claim: Poor lighting and long waiting times may add to feeling unsafe after dark, whatever the counts.
uncertainty: This is a hypothesis; no test has been run in the synthetic data.
assumptions: I assume the survey sample is comparable across quarters.
hypothesis: Perceived safety after dark depends partly on lighting and expected waiting time (hypothesis).
mechanism: People who expect a slow response or poor visibility avoid going out, which the survey would show as feeling unsafe.
test_that_would_disprove_it: If areas with good lighting and short waits show the same unsafe share, the hypothesis fails.
